title: Mexican Red Rice with Tomato, Peas and Carrots
summary: Toasted rice is simmered in a smooth tomato sauce until tender, with carrot and peas steamed gently on top, for a bright, savoury side that holds its shape and colour.
equipment: medium saucepan with a tight lid (2-3 litres)

ingredients.item: low-salt chicken or vegetable stock (check the label)
fine sea salt or table salt
medium carrot, cut into 5 mm dice
serrano or other green chilli, pricked with a fork

steps.title: Rinse and dry the rice
steps.text: Wash the rice in plenty of cold water, swishing it through with your fingers until the water runs almost clear. Drain well, then spread it out on the tea towel to dry for at least 5 minutes. Rice that's properly dry toasts evenly in the next step rather than steaming in its own dampness.

steps.title: Soften the onion and garlic
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the saucepan over medium-high heat, add the onion and cook for 3-5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for a final 30 seconds. Lift the onion and garlic out with the slotted spoon, leaving the oil behind in the pan, since you only want their flavour going into the sauce, not more oil.

steps.title: Blend the sauce smooth
steps.text: Add the onion and garlic to the blender with 60ml of the stock, the tomatoes and the salt, and blend until completely smooth. A fully smooth sauce coats the rice evenly later rather than leaving uneven patches of colour and flavour.

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pan over medium-high heat, then add the rice and cook for 5-8 minutes, stirring often, until it turns golden and smells toasty. Toasting roasts the surface starch on each grain, which is what keeps the finished rice light and separate instead of clumping together.

steps.title: Simmer in the tomato sauce
steps.text: Pour in the blended tomato sauce, which will splutter as it hits the hot pan, then stir and simmer for 3-5 minutes until it thickens noticeably. This short simmer cooks off some of the raw tomato edge before the rice takes on the bulk of the liquid.

steps.title: Add stock and vegetables
steps.text: Pour in the remaining 300ml stock and stir gently just once, then add the chilli and scatter the carrot and peas over the top without stirring them in. Bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to medium-low and cook for 12-18 minutes, until no liquid is visible on the surface and the rice smells fully cooked. Leaving the vegetables undisturbed on top means they steam gently in the rising heat rather than sinking in and turning the rice patchy or breaking up the grains underneath.

steps.title: Rest off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered, without stirring, for 10-20 minutes. This resting time lets the last of the moisture absorb evenly through the grains so the base isn't wet while the top is still dry.

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff the rice through with a fork, folding the peas and carrots in as you go, and lift out the chilli if you'd rather not serve it. Serve with the coriander scattered over and the lime wedges alongside for squeezing. The fresh lime cuts through the richness of the toasted rice and tomato.

tips: Dry the rinsed rice properly before toasting; wet grains steam instead of browning and the rice won't develop the same toasty flavour.
Don't stir once the carrot and peas go on top, as disturbing them traps steam unevenly and can leave patches of rice undercooked.
Blend the tomato sauce until completely smooth, since any lumps of skin will show up as uneven specks once the rice is cooked.
Give the rice its full resting time before fluffing; skipping this is the most common reason the base turns out wetter than the top.
Keep the heat at medium-low once the lid goes on, as rice simmered too fast tends to catch on the base before the centre is tender.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour, keeping for up to 24 hours. Reheat only once, until piping hot and 74°C at the centre, adding a splash of water to loosen it if needed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
